newsitem.title: UK: Closing overseas stock market indices.
newsitem.headline: Closing overseas stock market indices.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 leading stock index finished moderately higher, bolstered by strength in the large multinational companies that benefited from a vicious sell-off in the pound, traders and analysts said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,862.6, up 11.1 points, or 0.23 percent.

FRANKFURT - Stock prices climbed in late session trading, extending the strong gains put on during the market session as investors continued to direct funds toward Germany. The DAX-30 index closed at 4,371.16, up 53.52 points, or 1.24 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4,400.30, up 31.76 points, or 0.73 percent.
PARIS - Stocks closed lower, unable to hold late-afternoon gains made on the back of Wall Street's strength, traders said. The CAC-40 index closed at 3,022.20, down 3.74 points, or 0.12 percent.
ZURICH - Stocks ended higher, boosted by late European buying after Wall Street stocks staged gains in early U.S. trade. The Swiss market index closed at 5,888.0, up 41.0 points, or 0.70 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended higher as the yen's slump against the dollar spurred buying in major export-oriented issues such as electronics and cars, brokers said. The 225-stock Nikkei average closed at 20,575.26, up 185.72 points, or 0.91 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks inched to a slightly higher close, with a record-breaking performance by Hutchison Whampoa offset by profit-taking in HSBC Holdings, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,666.59, up 8.47 points, or 0.05 percent.

SYDNEY - The stock market ended 1.2 percent higher on continuing anticipation of an official interest rate cut, and dealers say the bullish sentiment may see the market surge to record highs. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,723.8, up 32.6 points, or 1.21 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial stocks finished at record highs as players anticipated that positive money supply and private-sector credit figures would point to a reduction in the country's high interest rates. The All-Stock index closed at 7,490.8, up 46.8 points, or 0.63 percent. The All Gold index closed at 990.8, up 21.0 points, 2.17 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 9,125.9, up 71.5 points, or 0.79 percent.
